chunks: From the first day its mother gives birth to it until the completion of the year, it is called 'Huwarun'. So when it enters the second year, it is called 'Ibn Makhaaz' because its mother had carried it. So when it enters the third year, it is called 'Ibn Laboon', and that is because its mother had given birth and milk had come for her. So when it enters the fourth year, the male is called 'Hiqq' and the female 'Hiqqah' because it has become worthy of being burdened.

So when it enters the fifth year, it is called 'Jadha''. So when it enters the sixth year, it is called 'Saniyy' because it has cast its front teeth. So when it enters the seventh year, it casts its four teeth and is called 'Rubaiyy'. So when it enters the eighth year, it casts the tooth after the four and is called 'Sadeys'. So when it enters the ninth year and drops its canine, it is called 'Bazil'. So when it enters the tenth year, it is 'Mukhliif', and there is no name for it after that.
And the ages from which Zakat is taken are from 'Bint Makhaaz' to 'Al-Jadha''.

key_terms.ابْنُ لَبُونٍ: A camel in its third year, named because its mother gave birth and produced milk
key_terms.ابْنُ مَخَاضٍ: A camel in its second year, named because its mother carried it
key_terms.الصَّدَقَة: Zakat (alms-tax), specifically referring to the livestock tax in this context
key_terms.جَذَعٌ: A camel in its fifth year
key_terms.حُوَارٌ: A young camel in its first year
key_terms.حِقٌّ: A male camel in its fourth year, worthy of being burdened

ai.seo_question: What are the specific age classifications of camels for Zakat in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the precise biological markers of camel aging, establishing the 'Bint Makhad' through 'Jadha'' age range as the standard for Zakat eligibility, a classification rooted in pre-Islamic Arab custom but codified by the Imams. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on 'urf' (customary practice) in deriving fiqh, ensuring that charitable obligations are calculated based on tangible, observable physical maturity rather than arbitrary timeframes. This precision underscores the practical application of divine law in agricultural economies, linking spiritual duty to economic reality.

en.hubeali: The years of the camel – From the first day its mother gives it birth up to the completion of the year (it is name as) ‘Al-Huwarun’. So when it enters into the second, it is named as ‘Ibn Makhaaz’, because its mother had carried it. So when it enter into the third years, it is named as ‘Ibn Laboun’, and that is because its mother had placed (gave birth) and milk has come for her. So when it enters into the fourth year, it’s male is named as ‘Hiqqa’, and its female as ‘Hiqqat’, because it is rightful that it be burdened upon.

So when it enters into the fifth year, it is named as ‘Jaz’an’. So when it enters into the sixth year, it is named as ‘Saniyya’, because it had cast its front teeth. So when it enters into the seventh year, it casts its four (teeth) and it is named as ‘Rubaiya’. And when it enters into the eight, it casts the teeth which are after the four, and it is named as ‘Sadeysa’. So when it enters into the ninth year and drops its canines, it is named a ‘Bazila’. So when it enters into the tenth year, so it is left behind, and there is no name for it after that. And the years which it would be seized from with regards to the charity (Zakāt), is from ‘Bint Makhaaz’ up to ‘Al Jaza’a’’. (P.s. – This is an explanation of the terminology and is not a Hadeeth).
